headline: Stagnant blocs, rising debt: a mild 2028 slump and frontier defaults

events: US extends sectoral tariffs to pharma and semiconductors; China widens rare-earth export licensing
Fed trims to 3.25% then pauses as core inflation sticks near 3%
Ukraine front freezes into a negotiated-but-unratified ceasefire line; sanctions stay
AI capex keeps rising but enterprise ROI disappoints outside software and customer service
Ethiopia-style restructuring drags; Bolivia misses a eurobond coupon
AI-infrastructure stocks correct ~30%; US capex slows and growth dips to 0.8%, a near-recession
Fed cuts to 2.5%; US deficit widens past 7% of GDP in an election year
US election produces divided government; tariffs stay as bipartisan 'security' policy
Euro area stagnates; France faces a spread spike and an ECB TPI-backed calm
Global unemployment peaks at 5.6% as youth joblessness rises in South Asia and North Africa
Recovery is shallow; Japan's long yields cross 3% and BoJ slows QT
Pakistan and Kenya enter IMF-led restructurings under the slow Common Framework
China grows ~3.5%, exports deflation via EV and solar overcapacity; EU raises anti-subsidy duties
Border clashes between two Sahel-adjacent states escalate into a sustained regional war
Record heat in South Asia cuts wheat yields; food inflation briefly lifts G20 CPI to 3.6%
Most NDCs for 2035 come in weak; emissions flat-to-slightly-down, coal stable in Asia
AI agents become standard in back offices; clerical hiring freezes rather than mass layoffs
US interest costs exceed defence spending; bond-market jitters force a modest fiscal package
Middle East tensions persist with periodic Red Sea shipping disruption
Protests over housing costs and pension reform in several European capitals
Global growth steadies near 2.7%; policy rates settle around 3%
WTO effectively sidelined; trade runs through bilateral and bloc deals
Global public debt passes 103% of GDP; US at ~133%
Warming 1-year average near 1.58C; 1.5C overshoot accepted as fact
Populist parties hold or share power in a majority of G7 countries

winners: India, Mexico and Vietnam as connector economies for supply-chain rerouting
Large AI platform and cloud firms that survived the 2028 correction with pricing power
Gulf states and commodity exporters of critical minerals
losers: Frontier-market debtors in Africa and South Asia squeezed by aid cuts and high rates
Young renters in Western cities facing unaffordable housing and thinner entry-level hiring
Export-dependent mid-sized European manufacturers caught between US tariffs and Chinese competition
bullets: Growth averages about 2.6%: no collapse, but a world running below its pre-2020 potential.
Trade is organised in overlapping blocs; tariffs are higher than in 2026 and treated as permanent.
Public debt keeps creeping up everywhere; interest bills crowd out investment and social spending.
AI is used by roughly a third of firms; it erodes clerical and junior white-collar hiring more than it causes visible layoffs.
Four sovereign restructurings in frontier economies proceed slowly, deepening resentment of Western creditors and China alike.
Climate policy lags: renewables reach ~42% of electricity, but emissions only plateau and 1.5C is being breached.
Trust in institutions slips further and unrest is higher, centred on housing, pensions and food prices.
A new regional war in Africa adds to frozen conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East, stretching humanitarian budgets that were already cut.
wildcard: A 2028 cyberattack attributed to a state proxy shut a major European port's logistics systems for nine days, accelerating 'sovereign cloud' mandates.
image_description: In a sweltering Karachi evening, a young graduate with an AI-tutoring app on a cracked phone queues outside a shuttered bank branch, while a container ship flagged to a bloc-friendly registry idles in the haze offshore.
